title: Make Athena's homepage lead with Athena, not the firstmate study
summary: The homepage (rendered by `cargo run -p xtask -- site` from studies/firstmate-work-handling/intro.json) is almost all firstmate study. For the newcomer audience, I read the goal as putting a visible Athena section first, with install and an example request, a real cost and a named checker model from a real job, and the firstmate study framed as a sample below it. The rating also flags a few header problems: a repo-internal study-id paragraph, firstmate used before it is explained, and the f1/f3 id gap.

defaults_applied.how: The final criterion ties success to a newcomer answering the four questions on the page, not to the activity of editing.
cargo test, clippy and fmt criteria.
Criteria render the real page and check its content.
One focused change to the site renderer and its data.
The design doc update is written for an outside reader.
Cost and model figures must trace to a committed source or be labeled as illustrative.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: I read xtask/src/site.rs (`render` at line 239 builds the header from intro.json `about`, then 'Start here'; `cites`, `intro_item` and `leadin` require each element to cite a known claim in claims.json; `load` reads the six study JSON files; `build` at line 628 writes index.html), studies/firstmate-work-handling/intro.json (`about.athena` is the only Athena text), and crates/athena-core/src/audience.rs (`validate_report`, `is_low`, `latest`, which handle the ratings that raised this). Resolution and probing order for the site: `build` loads the study, `render` checks claim ids, then writes the page. The change adds no record or data file under crates/, so `check_record_file`, `AnyRecord` and the round-trip test are untouched; any new study data file goes under studies/ and must be loaded by `load`. The property is measured directly by rendering the real study and checking the HTML, using the existing real-study tests in site.rs, such as `the_real_study_renders_with_an_intro_and_glossary`.
Goal and audience: a newcomer who opens https://doodla.github.io/athena/ and wants to learn about Athena. Three ratings of 3 in a row (094304-zwbs, 105301-jatx, 115412-c8ez) give the same findings.

Cost and checker evidence must come from a real committed source, such as a worked example from docs/ or README, or an existing study field. The producer must not invent numbers. If none exists, the page labels the example as illustrative and gives no figures.

The Athena sentences are not claims about firstmate, so they cannot cite claims.json. The producer may add a separate `athena` block that the renderer treats differently, and must keep the rule that firstmate sentences cite claims.
Install and example request text is copied from README.md, not rewritten from memory.
The f2 gap in the 'Limits of this study' ids is a display issue. Renumber or explain it, whichever is cheaper.
No governance file changes: athena.toml, defaults.toml and workflows are untouched. The deployed page updates through the existing site workflow, so nothing is needed there.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo run -p xtask -- site` and read the generated index.html. Before the 'Start here' section there is an Athena section containing an install command and an example request taken from README.md. Check with Grep on the output.

The generated index.html shows, for a real or explicitly labeled illustrative job, the producer model, a different checker model, and a cost figure. Any figure must trace to a committed file named in the page or the diff.

In the generated index.html, the firstmate study is introduced as a sample of Athena's output before 'Words used first', and 'firstmate' is explained in one plain sentence before the first defined term. The repo-internal 'study id ... folder under studies/' wording is gone from the header.

`cargo test -p xtask` passes, including new tests that render the real study and assert the Athena section, install command, model/cost lines and ordering. A render with a firstmate sentence that cites no claim is still an error.
`cargo clippy --all-targets` is clean and `cargo fmt --check` passes.
The ids in 'Limits of this study' are either consecutive or the gap is explained on the page, and the existing test `the_real_pages_limits_list_has_consecutive_finding_ids` agrees.
docs/design/explainer-site.md describes the new page order and where the Athena text comes from, with the alternative considered, so a stranger can follow it.

Outcome check: the page lets a newcomer answer 'what is Athena, how do I start, what did a job cost, which model checked it' without leaving the page. This is the property the next audience rating tests.

out_of_scope: Changing the firstmate study's claims, pin or model beyond wording needed for ordering
Changing audience rating records or the rating process in crates/
departures: Slightly higher cost and lower pass chance than the reference. Real cost and model evidence may not exist in committed files, and the renderer's every-sentence-cites-a-claim rule needs a design choice.
